claims.text: Spin-polarized DFT can be used to detect and predict ferromagnetic ground states in alloys with partially filled d-bands.
Allowing spin polarization captures exchange splitting.
Exchange splitting can lower the energy of a spin-aligned state relative to a nonmagnetic configuration.
The target material is a high-entropy alloy or intermetallic with a partly filled d-band configuration.
Comparing total energies from ferromagnetic, non-spin-polarized, and antiferromagnetic calculations can assess magnetic ground-state stability.
The computational setup must include spin degrees of freedom to represent electronic exchange interactions.
A partly filled d-band electronic structure enables exchange splitting when spin polarization is allowed.
Explicit treatment of electron spin in DFT can capture exchange stabilization of ferromagnetic ordering.
A spin-polarized state lying below a nonmagnetic state indicates magnetic stabilization.
The ferromagnetic configuration will have lower total energy than the nonmagnetic or differently ordered configurations.
The predicted ferromagnetic configuration will have a finite magnetic moment per atom.
Non-spin-polarized DFT does not show an energy gain from magnetic ordering.
Thermal disorder and alloy complexity may cause real materials to differ from idealized zero-temperature DFT predictions.
The choice of exchange-correlation functional may affect the accuracy of the magnetic prediction.
Disorder, correlation effects beyond standard functionals, and finite-temperature effects may weaken agreement between DFT predictions and experimental magnetism.
